tracks.title: Why do people buy gold?
tracks.note: 오늘 기사(구글 시가총액 급락)와 같은 '돈과 시장' 주제예요. 1회차는 대략적인 내용만, 2회차는 스크립트를 보면서 들어요.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: Hi Phil.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Hi Georgie.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: I've got a question for you.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Do you own anything made of gold?

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: Well, at the moment I'm wearing a lot of gold-coloured jewellery, but I'm not sure exactly how much of it is made of gold.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: OK.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: I don't think I own anything made of gold.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Beyond jewellery and other personal items, gold is bought and sold by investors and banks.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: The price of gold has always gone up and down, but in 2026 it reached its highest ever price.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: In this episode of 6 Minute English, we'll be talking about how gold became a valuable investment and asking the question, why do people buy gold?

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Let's start with our quiz question, Georgie.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Gold is a metal that's extracted or dug up from under the ground in mines.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: But how much gold has been extracted from the earth?

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Is it: a) over 50,000 tonnes, b) over 100,000 tonnes, or c) over 200,000 tonnes?

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: Phil, I have absolutely no idea, but I'm going to go with c) 200,000 tonnes.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: OK.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Well, we'll give you the answer at the end of the programme.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: OK Phil.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: So, we've been using gold for thousands of years, but why and how did it start?

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Well, before money was paper or plastic or just numbers in your bank account, a lot of it was actually gold.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: And experts have discovered gold in coins that are thought to have been made in the 6th Century BC.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: So, gold coins were made and they were used because the metal was much easier to carry and trade than things like cattle or timber.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: OK.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: But now our money isn't literally made of gold, so why is gold valuable?

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: It's a good question, but even though it isn't money, gold is still a financial asset, and an asset is something valuable that could be sold for money.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: And people buy gold in times of crisis because it's thought of as a safe investment.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Let's listen to expert Suki Cooper explaining more to the BBC World Service.

transcript.speaker: Suki Cooper
transcript.text: Gold is a safe haven because it's not connected to one particular government or one particular economy or one particular market, so the fact that it's neutral means it's an asset that's perceived to be a store of value over a longer term.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Suki describes gold as a safe haven, and a safe haven means something or somewhere that's protected from harm or danger, or in financial terms, from a fall in value.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: Yes, Suki explains that, unlike dollars or pounds for example, gold is not connected to a particular country.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: It's neutral.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: And Georgie, because we get gold from mines, there's more or less a fixed amount.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Unlike paper money, you can't just print more, as Catherine Schenk, professor of economic and social history, explains.

transcript.speaker: Catherine Schenk
transcript.text: It can't be created and fabricated out of thin air through alchemy, and so this, sort of, controls the supply and sustains an underlying value behind the demand for gold.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: Catherine explains that gold can't be created out of thin air, an expression meaning making something from nothing.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: As Catherine says, we don't make gold through alchemy.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Alchemy is an ancient kind of chemistry that attempted to do impossible things, like turn ordinary metals into gold.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: And because we can't just magically make more gold, when lots of people want to buy gold, the price increases.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: OK.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: Understood.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: Now, Phil, at the start of this programme, you said that gold prices hit an all-time high in early 2026.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: So, what's going on?

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Well, we mentioned that the price of gold increases in times of crisis because government banks want to buy more of it.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: And there has been a series of world events that have made government banks want to buy more gold, for example the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, and in politics too, for example the US imposing tariffs on international products.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: But since that peak in January, the price has dropped a bit.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: OK.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: And does the fall in the price of gold mean that people won't want to invest in it in the future?

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: It's likely that the price will go up again.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Experts believe that gold will always be an attractive investment during uncertain times.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Let's hear from market strategist John Reade.

transcript.speaker: John Reade
transcript.text: So much of the world we live in now is ethereal.

transcript.speaker: John Reade
transcript.text: It's... it's virtual, it's online, it disappears, whereas gold is something solid, something dependable and, you know, maybe something a little bit old fashioned.

transcript.speaker: John Reade
transcript.text: And maybe it's a hankering for traditional values rather than what is super modern and super changeable.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: John says that much of the modern world is ethereal, meaning it doesn't seem real.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: And in this ethereal world, people have a hankering for something that's solid and real, like gold.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: And the expression a hankering for means a strong desire for something.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: OK.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: Phil, I think it's time for the answer to your quiz question.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: OK.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Well, I asked how much gold has been mined from the ground to date.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: I said 200,000 tonnes.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: And that is the correct answer!

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: OK.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Let's recap the vocabulary we learnt in this programme, starting with asset.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: And an asset is something of financial value that can be sold for money.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: A safe haven is something or somewhere protected from harm or loss.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: To make something out of thin air is an expression meaning to make something from nothing.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: Alchemy is a kind of ancient chemistry that attempted to do impossible things, like making gold from ordinary metals.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: If something is ethereal, it doesn't seem real.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: And if you have a hankering for something, you have a strong desire for it.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Once again, our six minutes are up, and if you have a hankering for more practice, test what you've learned with the worksheet on our website.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: That's bbclearningenglish.com.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: Thank you for joining us.

transcript.speaker: Georgie
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Phil
transcript.text: Goodbye!

listening.task: 6 Minute English를 한 번은 대략적인 내용만 듣고, 두 번째는 스크립트를 보면서 들어요. 그다음 퀴즈에 답해 보세요. 'safe haven'이 나오는 부분을 잘 들어 보세요. 시간이 남으면 The Daily로 이어가요.

quiz.q: How much gold has been extracted from the earth? a) over 50,000 tonnes, b) over 100,000 tonnes, c) over 200,000 tonnes
quiz.answer: c) over 200,000 tonnes. 보너스: 금이 'safe haven'인 이유는 특정 정부·경제·시장에 묶여 있지 않은 중립 자산이라서예요. 금화는 기원전 6세기쯤 처음 만들어졌어요 (소나 목재보다 들고 다니며 거래하기 쉬웠으니까요).

sentences.text: But how much gold has been extracted from the earth?
sentences.ko: 그런데 지금까지 땅에서 캐낸 금은 얼마나 될까요?

sentences.text: Well, we'll give you the answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.ko: 음, 정답은 프로그램 마지막에 알려 드릴게요.

sentences.text: And Georgie, because we get gold from mines, there's more or less a fixed amount.
sentences.ko: 그리고 조지, 금은 광산에서 캐내기 때문에 양이 거의 정해져 있어요.

sentences.text: It's likely that the price will go up again.
And the expression a hankering for means a strong desire for something.
sentences.ko: 그리고 'a hankering for'라는 표현은 무언가를 강하게 원한다는 뜻이에요.

reading.title: Google's $500bn bloodbath reflects the danger it faces from AI
reading.summaryKo: 검색 광고 성장이 5분기 만에 가장 느려지자 알파벳 시가총액이 하루에 5천억 달러(12%) 증발했어요. AI 챗봇이 구글 검색 사업을 위협하고 있고, AI를 더 빨리 활용한 메타가 곧 세계 최대 광고 매출 기업이 될 수 있다는 글이에요.
excerpt: Soon after Chatgpt first captured the world's attention four years ago, some investors began to fret that clever chatbots would upend one of the most lucrative businesses to have emerged in decades: Google search. For a time these concerns seemed unfounded, with the firm's ad sales showing little sign of slowing. On October 29th, however, the fears returned with a vengeance, as Alphabet, Google's parent company, shed $500bn of market value, 12% of its total, in a single trading session following disappointing quarterly earnings the previous day.

In the three months from July to September Google's ad revenue from search and other businesses grew by 11%, year on year, the slowest pace in five quarters. A strong performance at the company's cloud arm did little to assuage investors. Before long Meta, which has been quicker to harness artificial intelligence to boost its advertising business, may overtake the search giant as the world's biggest generator of ad revenue.
reading.tip: 전체 기사는 Economist 구독 계정으로 읽어 보세요. 돈·시장 표현에 주목: shed $500bn of market value (시가총액이 증발하다), with a vengeance (더 거세게), assuage investors (투자자를 안심시키다), overtake (추월하다).

vocab.example: Some investors began to fret that chatbots would hurt Google search.
AI could upend the way we look for information.
The fears returned with a vengeance.
Alphabet shed $500bn of market value in a single day.
Strong cloud sales did little to assuage investors.

vocab.meaning: 안전 자산, 피난처 (오늘 BBC 금 에피소드)
vocab.example: In a crisis, many investors see gold as a safe haven.

writing.prompt: Do you still use Google search, or do you ask an AI chatbot? Write 4–5 sentences in English.
writing.question: When do you use Google, and when do you use an AI chatbot? Which one do you trust more?
writing.hint: 이런 표현을 써 보세요: These days I mostly ... / When I need ..., I ... / I still prefer ... because ... / The problem with ... is that ... / I'd rather ...

speaking.prompt: In one minute, tell a friend: would you buy gold or tech stocks right now? Why?
speaking.alt: 쉬운 버전: Do you own anything made of gold? Tell me about it.

evening.note: 사흘째예요! 어제 이어서 10페이지. 습관이 잡히는 중이니 피곤하면 5페이지만 읽어도 충분해요.
